teams.heading: Mark Nawaqanitawase's Test choice stays open as Wallabies captain offers verdict
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase has not yet officially committed his Test future to Fiji or Australia. Fresh headlines include a Wallabies captain's verdict on his future, headlined ‘It’s pretty obvious’, and an ESPN piece on Wallabies interest in his return to rugby, headlined ‘A freak’. Sir Steve Hansen has said he would be better off playing for Fiji, a view reported at the weekend.

teams.heading: Borthwick calls up Spencer and Randall as injuries sideline Mitchell, McParland
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has added Ben Spencer (19 caps) and Harry Randall (14) to England's Nations Championship squad after injuries ruled Northampton's Alex Mitchell and uncapped Archie McParland out of the Australia match. Mitchell pulled up with a hamstring issue on top of three earlier hamstring injuries this year and faces a scan, while McParland, 21, picked up a calf injury at last week's three-day camp. Fin Smith's calf problem also opens up fly-half, with Marcus Smith and George Ford competing to deputise.

lead.why: A fresh squad change and injury news ahead of the Australia Test, which is squad news about England's own players and outranks the Edwards feature.

teams.heading: Galthié adds five to his 42-man France squad, including uncapped Léon Darricarrère
teams.body: Five new names have come into Fabien Galthié's 42-man group. Clermont prop Régis Montagne replaces Bayonne's Tevita Tatafu, and Toulouse scrumhalf Paul Graou comes in for La Rochelle's Nolann Le Garrec, who has suffered another hamstring injury. Florian Verhaeghe, Rodrigue Neti and uncapped Clermont centre Léon Darricarrère complete the additions. France host the Springboks at the Stade de France and Argentina there on 21 November.

lead.why: A fresh squad change with named incomers, a replacement for an injured scrumhalf, and an uncapped centre, which is the kind of selection news a fan would text about.

teams.heading: Ireland great Cian Healy rejoins Leinster as full-time player development officer
teams.body: Healy has taken a full-time post with Leinster, working with the province's most promising young players as an elite player development officer. He started the job last month after coaching with Clontarf in the All-Ireland League and Belvedere College since retiring in 2025. He filled in on Leinster's matchday coaching staff for last weekend's URC win over Connacht, covering for Seán O'Brien, who was on leave after the birth of his daughter. Leo Cullen's verdict: "Cian is in the building with us now, which is fantastic."

lead.why: It is a new, concrete development with a named coach quote, and it is the most talked-about Irish item in today's pack.

teams.heading: Italy call up ex-Pumas flyhalf Domingo Miotti for Springboks Test
teams.body: Montpellier flyhalf Domingo Miotti has been included in Quesada's 33-man squad for Saturday's Test against South Africa in Turin, the former Argentina No 10 qualifying through an Italian grandfather. His last Argentina Test came in 2022, and he gives Quesada a fourth flyhalf option alongside Paolo Garbisi, Tommaso Allan and Giacomo Da Re. Quesada said: "Domingo is a great player and an excellent person." He was unavailable last week through injury but can now resume training as normal.

lead.why: A fresh squad selection that adds a new flyhalf option to Italy's 33-man group, with a named player and a coach quote.

teams.heading: Townsend loses Ritchie and Millar Mills, calls up uncapped Blyth-Lafferty
teams.body: Scotland's New Zealand build-up has lost two forwards from the extended squad. Jamie Ritchie, who joined Glasgow from Perpignan this summer, came off early in Glasgow's win over the Lions with an injury, while Newcastle prop Elliot Millar Mills went off after minutes of Newcastle's defeat. Replacing them are uncapped Edinburgh prop Ollie Blyth-Lafferty, fellow Edinburgh prop D'Arcy Rae and Edinburgh back-rower Freddy Douglas, with Sale scrum-half Gus Warr also training this week.

lead.why: A fresh squad and injury event that directly affects Scotland's build-up to the All Blacks, with two outlets corroborating it.

teams.heading: URC threatens WRU with legal action over Premiership talks for Welsh clubs
teams.body: WalesOnline understands the URC has written to the WRU telling it not to enter formal discussions with the RFU or Premiership Rugby, and has threatened legal action if those talks continue. The competition insists Wales keep four sides, and the WRU, an equal shareholder, is contractually obliged to supply them. Abi Tierney confirmed the English talks at a Professional Rugby Board meeting last week, and the Ospreys and Scarlets remain in the firing line over the three-team plan.

lead.why: It is a new development with direct consequences for Welsh clubs and the WRU, and it is more pressing than the club-derby and pundit items.

teams.heading: Ex-Pumas flyhalf Domingo Miotti called up by Italy for Springboks Test
teams.body: Italy coach Gonzalo Quesada has picked Domingo Miotti in a 33-man squad, a 30-year-old Montpellier flyhalf whose last of 10 Tests for Argentina came on 9 July 2022. Miotti qualifies through an Italian grandfather, and Quesada says their contact began three years ago. "Domingo is a great player and an excellent person." Italy also host Argentina this month, and Miotti, injured last week, can now resume training as normal.

lead.why: A former Pumas flyhalf switching to Italy is a concrete new event, and Italy host Argentina this month.

teams.heading: Les Kiss explains Pietsch omission as Wallabies turn to experience
teams.body: Les Kiss has gone into the reasons for leaving Pietsch out and the fullback contest that follows. The clearest sign of the experience push is Kurtley Beale, 37, named in the touring party after five years away from international rugby and added once Hunter Paisami made himself unavailable for personal reasons. "No one comes in just to fill a void," Kiss said, placing Beale at 12 with the chance to flex to 15 and 10. Former All Black Jeff Wilson has called the move backwards.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item about the Wallabies' own squad selection, and it is not a repeat of the Crichton, Beale or World Cup stories already run.

teams.heading: Suntory circle as Stormers open extension talks with Damian Willemse
teams.body: Suntory Sungoliath are reportedly "showing great interest" in Springbok full-back Damian Willemse, with Rapport reporting they are ready to spend "a lot of yen" to land him in Tokyo. The Stormers are not waiting: a source told the paper the extension process has already begun, with broad principles and amounts agreed. Willemse is in the final year of the five-year deal he signed in 2022 and could move to Japan only after the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Suntory already have Sam Cane and James Lowe on their payroll.

lead.why: The only men's 15s item in the pack with a Japan angle; candidates 2 to 4 are WXV women's matches and excluded, and the other Willemse coverage is the story already run on Monday.

teams.heading: Matfield warns All Blacks Scotland could be bigger test than England
teams.body: Speaking on the Rugby Rivals podcast, former Springbok lock Victor Matfield said Scotland "might actually be a bigger challenge than England", pointing to Glasgow, unbeaten, and Edinburgh, unbeaten before a Benetton loss. He said Scotland are playing nice rugby. Former All Blacks winger John Kirwan agreed Scotland would pose a serious threat, recalling New Zealand's 25-17 win at Murrayfield last year after they led 17-0 early, and said the All Blacks are motivated to avenge the 33-19 Twickenham defeat to England.

lead.why: The most-covered New Zealand angle in today's pack, a pundit warning that puts Scotland's form at the centre of the All Blacks' preparation for the Murrayfield test.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus names experienced Italy match 23, with Salmaan Moerat back
teams.body: Erasmus has gone with experience for Saturday's Nations Championship Test against Italy, and none of the six uncapped squad players makes the match 23. Riley Norton, Yaqeen Ahmed and Markus Muller are in camp, with Erasmus hoping to give them a chance later on tour. Salmaan Moerat is the only newcomer to the green and gold this season, back from neck and toe injuries that kept him out of the first leg.

lead.why: A fresh official match 23 naming for the Italy Test, with concrete player decisions, is the strongest new selection news.
